findings.body:
`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with an f-string built from `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` is command injection. A value like `name="; id > /tmp/pwned #"` (or similar metacharacters in `upload_dir` / `oid`) runs arbitrary shell commands as the converter user.

ImageMagick policy delegates do not require a shell from Python — keep the argv-list form so each path is a single literal argument:

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

If IM7 needs an explicit policy file, pass it as a separate argv element (e.g. `[-policy`, `path`, ...]`), still without `shell=True`.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change introduces shell command injection in `make_thumb`.

## Narrative

The previous implementation used the argv-list form of `subprocess.run`, which does not invoke a shell and treats each argument as a literal. The new code builds a single shell string from `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`, then runs it with `shell=True`.

Any of those values containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, `$()`, backticks, spaces/globs, etc.) can execute arbitrary commands as the process user. The removed comment claimed `name` was validated upstream; even if that still holds for `name`, `upload_dir` and `oid` are interpolated the same way and are not shown to be validated here. Dropping the `/usr/bin/convert` absolute path also makes the call depend on `PATH`.

ImageMagick 7 policy/delegate configuration does not require `shell=True` from Python. Keep the argv list (or pass a fixed policy via argv/env) so paths never reach a shell.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: thumbs.py now runs `subprocess.run` with `shell=True` and an f-string that interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`, so shell metacharacters in those values execute as the converter user. The base revision used a safe argv-list form; this change introduced the injection.
